title: Enhancing biological removal of high-strength TMAH using dissolved encapsulated sulfur in SBR and MBR systems
description: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH), a toxic organic nitrogen compound widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, is challenging to treat biologically at high concentrations because of microbial inhibition and process instability. This study investigated dissolved encapsulated sulfur (DES) as a functional medium for stabilizing aerobic TMAH biodegradation in sequencing batch reactor (SBR) and membrane bioreactor (MBR) systems. DES-amended reactors were first compared with corresponding DES-free controls and subsequently operated under stepwise increases in TMAH concentration up to 2,000 mg/L. DES addition substantially improved TMAH removal in both reactor configurations. At 2,000 mg/L, the DES-amended MBR achieved an average TMAH removal efficiency of 95%, compared with 71% in the DES-amended SBR during the final operational period. TMAH degradation was accompanied by NH4+-N accumulation and changes in NO2--N and NO3--N, indicating altered nitrogen transformation under high-strength loading. A net sulfate increase was observed after correction for measured influent sulfate concentrations, consistent with net sulfur oxidation associated with DES operation. The MBR maintained a greater biomass inventory and volumetric TMAH removal capacity than the SBR, without consistently higher apparent mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS)-normalized removal rates. Microbial community profiling revealed temporal shifts in the MBR, with transient enrichment of Microbacterium and Methyloversatilis and late-stage predominance of Hyphomicrobium, genera potentially involved in TMAH biodegradation and downstream methylated C1-compound metabolism. These results indicate that DES contributed to a reaction environment favorable for aerobic TMAH biodegradation, while membrane-based biomass retention supported stable treatment under high-strength loading.
